title: Exchange followed by point transport: composition and change of representative
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal B,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ and $V:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ functors. For integers $r\geq1$ let $P_r$ and $Q_r$ be endofunctors of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal B$, respectively. For $m\geq1$ supply natural isomorphisms $c_m:P_1P_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{m+1}$ and $t_m:Q_1Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{m+1}$. Here juxtaposition of functors means composition, the rightmost acting first.

Supply natural transformations $\iota^{(r)}:V\to VQ_r$ such that for every $N\in\mathcal B$ and $m\geq1$,
$$\iota_N^{(m+1)}=V(t_{m,N})\circ\iota_{Q_mN}^{(1)}\circ\iota_N^{(m)}.$$
Supply natural transformations $e_r:Q_rF\to FP_r$ satisfying, for all $M\in\mathcal C$ and $m\geq1$,
$$e_{m+1,M}\circ t_{m,FM}=F(c_{m,M})\circ e_{1,P_mM}\circ Q_1(e_{m,M}).$$
Set $H=VF$ and $\tau^F_{r,M}=V(e_{r,M})\circ\iota^{(r)}_{FM}:H(M)\to H(P_rM)$. Then $\tau^F_r$ is natural in $M$, and
$$\tau^F_{m+1,M}=H(c_{m,M})\circ\tau^F_{1,P_mM}\circ\tau^F_{m,M}.$$

Moreover, for any functor $F_d:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ and specified natural isomorphism $C:F_d\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, define
$$e^d_{r,M}=C_{P_rM}^{-1}\circ e_{r,M}\circ Q_r(C_M),\qquad \tau^d_{r,M}=V(e^d_{r,M})\circ\iota^{(r)}_{F_dM}.$$
Then
$$\tau^d_{r,M}=V(C_{P_rM}^{-1})\circ\tau^F_{r,M}\circ V(C_M),$$
and these maps satisfy
$$\tau^d_{m+1,M}=(VF_d)(c_{m,M})\circ\tau^d_{1,P_mM}\circ\tau^d_{m,M}.$$
No invertibility of $e_r$ or $\iota^{(r)}$ and no morphism $P_1M\to M$ is assumed.

A functor preserves identities and composition. A natural transformation is a family of component maps commuting with every morphism; a natural isomorphism is such a family with invertible components.

proof.text: Fix $r\geq1$ and $f:M\to N$. Naturality of $e_r$ gives $F(P_r f)\circ e_{r,M}=e_{r,N}\circ Q_r(Ff)$; naturality of $\iota^{(r)}$ gives $V(Q_r(Ff))\circ\iota^{(r)}_{FM}=\iota^{(r)}_{FN}\circ V(Ff)$. Apply $V$ to the first equality and compose with the second. Functoriality and associativity [def-nagata-category] give $H(P_rf)\circ\tau^F_{r,M}=\tau^F_{r,N}\circ H(f)$, proving naturality.

proof.text:
Fix $m\geq1$ and $M$. Substitute the assumed point composition law into the definition of $\tau^F_{m+1,M}$, combine the first two factors using functoriality of $V$, and substitute the assumed exchange law. This gives
$$\tau^F_{m+1,M}=H(c_{m,M})\circ V(e_{1,P_mM})\circ V(Q_1(e_{m,M}))\circ\iota^{(1)}_{Q_mFM}\circ\iota^{(m)}_{FM}.$$
Naturality of $\iota^{(1)}$ at the actual morphism $e_{m,M}:Q_mFM\to FP_mM$ says
$$V(Q_1(e_{m,M}))\circ\iota^{(1)}_{Q_mFM}=\iota^{(1)}_{FP_mM}\circ V(e_{m,M}).$$
Insert this equality and reassociate [def-nagata-category]. The two adjacent pairs are exactly $\tau^F_{1,P_mM}$ and $\tau^F_{m,M}$, yielding the required recurrence.

proof.text:
For the supplied natural isomorphism $C:F_d\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, naturality of $\iota^{(r)}$ at $C_M:F_dM\to FM$ is
$$V(Q_r(C_M))\circ\iota^{(r)}_{F_dM}=\iota^{(r)}_{FM}\circ V(C_M).$$
Expand $e^d_{r,M}$ in $\tau^d_{r,M}$, distribute $V$ over the three-factor composite, and insert this equality. Associativity [def-nagata-category] and the definition of $\tau^F$ give
$$\tau^d_{r,M}=V(C_{P_rM}^{-1})\circ\tau^F_{r,M}\circ V(C_M).$$

proof.text:
Put $A_T=V(C_T)$ and $H_d=VF_d$. Functoriality gives $A_T^{-1}=V(C_T^{-1})$ by applying $V$ to both inverse identities. Naturality of $C$ at $c_{m,M}:P_1P_mM\to P_{m+1}M$ gives
$$H_d(c_{m,M})\circ A_{P_1P_mM}^{-1}=A_{P_{m+1}M}^{-1}\circ H(c_{m,M}).$$
Using step 3 twice and cancelling only $A_{P_mM}\circ A_{P_mM}^{-1}$, associativity [def-nagata-category] gives
$$H_d(c_{m,M})\circ\tau^d_{1,P_mM}\circ\tau^d_{m,M}=A_{P_{m+1}M}^{-1}\circ H(c_{m,M})\circ\tau^F_{1,P_mM}\circ\tau^F_{m,M}\circ A_M.$$
By step 2 this is $A_{P_{m+1}M}^{-1}\circ\tau^F_{m+1,M}\circ A_M$, which is $\tau^d_{m+1,M}$ by step 3. All cancellations used components of $C$ alone; $e_r$ and $\iota^{(r)}$ were used only as morphisms.

lean.statement: theorem exchange_transport_composition_conjugation (F : C ⥤ B) (V : B ⥤ D) (P : ℕ+ → C ⥤ C) (Q : ℕ+ → B ⥤ B) (c : ∀ m : ℕ+, P m ⋙ P 1 ≅ P (m + 1)) (t : ∀ m : ℕ+, Q m ⋙ Q 1 ≅ Q (m + 1)) (ι : ∀ r : ℕ+, V ⟶ Q r ⋙ V) (e : ∀ r : ℕ+, F ⋙ Q r ⟶ P r ⋙ F) (hι : ∀ (m : ℕ+) (N : B), (ι (m + 1)).app N = (ι m).app N ≫ (ι 1).app ((Q m).obj N) ≫ V.map ((t m).hom.app N)) (he : ∀ (m : ℕ+) (M : C), (t m).hom.app (F.obj M) ≫ (e (m + 1)).app M = (Q 1).map ((e m).app M) ≫ (e 1).app ((P m).obj M) ≫ F.map ((c m).hom.app M)) : (∀ (m : ℕ+) (M : C), (exchangePointTransport F V (ι (m + 1)) (e (m + 1))).app M = (exchangePointTransport F V (ι m) (e m)).app M ≫ (exchangePointTransport F V (ι 1) (e 1)).app ((P m).obj M) ≫ (F ⋙ V).map ((c m).hom.app M)) ∧ (∀ (Fd : C ⥤ B) (a : Fd ≅ F), (∀ (r : ℕ+) (M : C), (exchangePointTransport Fd V (ι r) (conjugatedExchange a (e r))).app M = V.map (a.hom.app M) ≫ (exchangePointTransport F V (ι r) (e r)).app M ≫ V.map (a.inv.app ((P r).obj M))) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ+) (M : C), (exchangePointTransport Fd V (ι (m + 1)) (conjugatedExchange a (e (m + 1)))).app M = (exchangePointTransport Fd V (ι m) (conjugatedExchange a (e m))).app M ≫ (exchangePointTransport Fd V (ι 1) (conjugatedExchange a (e 1))).app ((P m).obj M) ≫ (Fd ⋙ V).map ((c m).hom.app M)))
lean.note: The two auxiliary definitions give the actual natural transport and conjugated exchange maps. Naturality of the transport is built into its NatTrans type; the theorem states both recurrence laws and representative conjugacy. Positive indices are PNat, with no degree-zero datum.
